Article content: {"cover_media":"3_2082922526124982272","media_entities":["3_2082924778378190848","13_2082925267643731968","13_2082925528432902144"],"plain_text":"You wake up. Stretch. Get ready. You open your front door. Fresh air fills your lungs. Sunlight floods your eyes. You put your AirPods in: "Hey GPT..." knowing that for the next 3-4 hours of your morning you don't need to type a single email, write a single bit of text, or scroll a pointless feed. In fact, you can do all the low value time consuming work with ease in the morning with GPT voice so that you can become high agency. ONLY... if you set it up correctly. 
I'm writing this with quite a bit of enthusiasm.
It's one of the few things that has excited me recently.
When I write with enthusiasm there's often grammar and spelling mistakes... WHO GIVES A FUGG?
I want you to have the information to do this, it won't be pretty, it will be useful, so bookmark this fugging article and let's get into it.
KEY (so you don't get lost): text that is bold and in capital letters are HEADINGS, and SUBHEADINGS, text that is just bold are guides within the guide, you'll see what I mean in just 1 second.
HOW TO USE GPT VOICE TO CHANGE YOUR LIFE:
A: LOCAL COMPUTER
This isn’t a necessary step, but, you are going to be giving AI access to your computer.
You don’t want this (well I certainly don’t) to be your main computer as the risks that something might go wrong or some data being leaked begin to increase significantly.
There’s going to be a risk regardless, but having a separate computer that hasn’t got all your bank cards saved alongside your crypto that you can leave on to do remote work is the smart idea here.
2: SECOND BRAIN
This was popularised a long time ago in 2017 by Tiago Forte and subsequently 2022 when he released a book, but now with AI this idea is more useful than ever. So here’s how you set one up:
I have used AI here to put this process into concise bullet points for you to follow:
1: Understand why you need a second brain
AI can improve productivity, but it can also increase workloads and expectations.
A second brain helps you use AI effectively without feeling overwhelmed.
The goal is to create a system that stores your knowledge and makes it easier to think, decide and act.
2: Create one place for your knowledge
Store your notes, thoughts, ideas, decisions and projects in one digital place.
Use Obsidian, Apple Notes, Notion, Google Docs or plain text files.
The app matters less than using it consistently.
Plain text and Markdown are useful because you own the files and AI can easily read them.
3: Capture information before organising it
Start with a 15-minute brain dump.
Write down your:
Projects
Tasks
Decisions
Questions
Lessons
Ideas
Use daily notes, voice notes, meeting transcripts or journalling.
Do not edit or organise yet. First, get the information out of your head.
4: Organise for useful context
Start with a simple structure:
Projects: active work with a clear outcome
Areas: ongoing responsibilities
Resources: useful reference material
Archives: completed or inactive work
You can also add an inbox, daily notes and meeting notes.
Keep related information together.
Link connected people, meetings, projects and ideas.
Add folders only when necessary.
Organise for better AI context, not perfect tidiness.
5: Let AI distil your notes
Ask AI to:
Summarise key themes
Extract decisions and actions
Find recurring problems and connections
Highlight unanswered questions
Create weekly or monthly reviews
Compare current work with long-term goals
Let AI handle reading, sorting and summarising. You focus on what the information means.
6: Turn your knowledge into useful work
Always review AI-generated output.
Correct errors, add missing context and apply your own judgement.
Use your notes to create:
Emails
Plans
Project updates
Strategy documents
Decisions
Performance reviews
Daily briefs
Give AI clear instructions and relevant context.
Treat it like a capable employee: brief it, review its work and refine the result.
AI provides structure and synthesis. You remain responsible for the final decision.
7: Build the habit gradually
Your first 30 minutes:
5 minutes: create your second-brain folder
15 minutes: complete a brain dump
5 minutes: create the basic structure
5 minutes: ask AI to summarise the notes and identify patterns
Your first week:
Capture something every day.
Keep one daily note as a scratchpad.
Save useful ideas, meetings and decisions.
Ask AI to review the week.
Check what it understood and what it missed.
Export motes as markdown to make it easier.
Choose a note app, use obsidian as it’s AI friendly and local.
3: CONNECT GPT
 
Bosh.
OKAY. WE’RE ALMOST THERE.
SOON YOU’LL WAKE UP.
WALK OUT THE DOOR.
LOAD GPT VOICE UP.
AND GET YOUR BORING WORK DONE WHILST DRIVING TO A COFFEE DATE, OR WALKING TO THE BEACH, OR SUN BATHING IN THE GARDEN.
BUT WE GOT A BIT MORE TO DO SO ITS SET UP TO ME MAXXXXXXXIMUMLY USEFUL TO YOU.
ahhhhhhhhhhh, let's continue...
4: OTHER IMPORTANT CONNECTIONS
This is for you to figure out, but if you use any of the following as part of your day to day.
CONNECT THEM:
 
5: PUTTING IT ALL TOGETHER
We’re doing this so you can plug your headphones in and be this guy whilst doing your work - don’t forget why you’re here bro…
 
1: Update both apps
On your computer:
Install or update the new ChatGPT desktop app.
Sign in using the same account as your iPhone.
The app should show:
Chat
Work
Codex
On your iPhone:
Update the ChatGPT app.
Look for a Remote tab or remote-computer option.
The new desktop app is available on macOS and Windows, while Codex Remote is available across ChatGPT plans.
2: Choose Work or Codex
Use Work for:
Documents
Research
Browser tasks
Emails and connected services
Organising files
Your second brain
General knowledge work
Use Codex for:
Working with local folders
Running terminal commands
Editing files
Building automations
Coding
More technical computer workflows
Work can access local files and desktop applications when your account, region and permissions support it. Codex can work with local folders, repositories, terminals and developer tools.
3: Grant computer permissions
When prompted, allow ChatGPT access to:
Microphone
Accessibility
Screen and audio recording
The folders you want it to use
Supported applications
Notifications
On a Mac, these permissions are normally under:
System Settings → Privacy & Security
Enable ChatGPT under:
Accessibility
Screen & System Audio Recording
Microphone
These permissions allow ChatGPT to understand what is happening on the screen and interact with permitted applications.
Do not initially grant access to your entire drive. Start with one dedicated folder such as:
Second Brain
4: Enable Remote Control
Inside the ChatGPT desktop app or Codex section:
Open Settings.
Find Remote Control, Remote, or Device connections.
Enable discovery and remote control.
Ask it to display the pairing QR code.
The exact wording may differ slightly between app versions.
On your iPhone:
Open ChatGPT.
Open Remote.
Select Connect computer.
Scan the QR code displayed on your computer.
Approve the pairing on both devices.
Remote Control uses authenticated one-to-one QR pairing between the phone and computer.
5: Keep the computer available
For remote access to work, the computer generally needs to remain:
Powered on
Connected to the internet
Running the ChatGPT desktop app
Signed into your account
Available as a remote host
Some supported Mac configurations can continue limited computer-use workflows while locked, but availability depends on your account and region.
Disable automatic sleep while testing:
Mac: System Settings → Lock Screen/Energy
Windows: Settings → System → Power & battery
You can still allow the display to turn off.
6: Start GPT Voice
On the computer:
Open Work or Codex.
Press the Voice control.
Allow microphone access.
Begin a voice conversation.
YOU HAVE DONE IT...
BUT WHY IS GPT VOICE SO GOOD?
An AI second brain allows you to move beyond the limitations of your own memory, your own attention and your own administrative capacity.
No. You are not using AI to stop thinking, you're using it to remove low-value bullish*t work so that you can be higher agency.
Most people get ruled by these mundane tasks that wear you down, GPT voice helps to serve you and take that away so you can focus on higher value tasks at hand.
It gives you the chance to walk which is one of the best things you can do for creative thinking whilst increasing your capacity to act by turning idea to action rapidly so when you're back you're ready to shred.
Remember. You are the pilot. You control the system. The system does not control you.
You capture everything you think.
You stop relying on memory.
You start to bring order to the chaos.
You turn scattered knowledge into usable intelligence.
You connect ideas that would disappear.
You remove the sh*t work that drains your energy.
You preserve your attention for high agency tasks.
You direct the machine.
You own your knowledge.
You use the tools of your age instead of being overwhelmed by them.
You move from thought to action while the idea is still alive.
You become more capable.
You speak.
Your system captures.
Your system organises.
Your system acts.
You command.
YES. YES. YES. YES.
I swear, if you did not leave this article feeling absolutely pumped then I have not done my job in expressing how I truly feel about this. 
If you feel pumped (like me) then pump my like button (no homo).
AHHHHHHHHHHHH.
